introduction: Today we celebrate the Epiphany of the Lord, the manifestation of Christ to all the nations. Guided by a star, wise men from the East come to Bethlehem, worship the child, and offer gold, frankincense and myrrh. Isaiah calls Jerusalem to arise and shine, and Paul declares that the Gentiles are now fellow heirs of God's promise. As we gather, let us bring our own gifts to Christ, the light of every people.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Christ has been revealed as the light of all nations. Let us pray for the whole human family.
intentions: For the Church: that she may welcome every nation and culture, and make Christ known as the light of all peoples. Let us pray to the Lord.
For missionaries and for the young churches of the world: that they may grow in faith, in courage and in love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are searching for truth and meaning: that, like the Magi, they may follow the light that leads to Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For migrants and travellers far from home: that they may find welcome and protection. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our parish: that we may offer Christ the gifts of our faith, our prayer and our love. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Father of light, you revealed your Son to the nations by the guidance of a star. Hear our prayers, and lead all peoples to the joy of knowing him. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Gifts for the King
reflection.body:
"Arise, shine; for your light has come." Isaiah's words were first spoken to a ruined Jerusalem, after the exile. He pictures the city flooded with light, and nations coming from far away, bringing gold and frankincense to praise the Lord.

On the feast of the Epiphany we see that prophecy begin to come true. Wise men from the East, probably astrologers from Persia or Babylon, have studied the sky and seen a new star. They set out on a long journey to find the newborn king. They are not Jews. They do not know the Scriptures. Yet God speaks to them in the language they understand, the language of the stars, and leads them to Christ.

Paul calls this "the mystery" now revealed: "that the Gentiles are fellow heirs and fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of his promise in Christ Jesus." The child of Bethlehem is not only the Messiah of Israel; he is the Saviour of the whole world. The word "epiphany" means manifestation: Christ shown to all peoples.

Matthew also notices who does not come. King Herod is frightened and plots to kill the child. The chief priests know exactly where the Messiah is to be born but do not travel the few miles to see him. Knowledge without seeking leaves people where they are. The Magi, who knew far less, went and found him.

When they saw the star again, "they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy." Entering the house, they "fell down and worshiped him," and opened their treasures. Christian tradition has seen meaning in their gifts: gold for a king, frankincense for God, and myrrh for one who would die.

We too are invited to find Christ and to offer him our treasures. Our gold may be our time and resources; our incense, our prayer; our myrrh, the sufferings we unite to his. And like the Magi, after meeting him, we may need to go home by another way.
